title: ICE cotton ends lower on profit taking, stronger US dollar
content:
ICE December 2026 cotton settled at 83.86 cents, down 0.54 cent, after a 487-point gain in seven sessions.
Trading volume fell to 46,070 contracts, while open interest rose 3,575 to 343,058, signalling fresh positions despite lower prices.
US crop good ratings slipped to 40 per cent; West Texas weather, India monsoon, China's State Reserve buying and tight ICE stocks support cotton.

title: China's FDY correction opens a buying window before restocking
content:
Domestic-China FDY polyester filament yarn prices closed August 3–7, 2026 broadly lower across three benchmark deniers, Fibre2Fashion TexPro data showed.
The coarser 100D/72F led the correction at 3.35 per cent; 75D/36F softened 1.93 per cent and 150D/96F fell 1.43 per cent.
The fall ended July’s fluctuating-upward trend and shifted the domestic price centre firmly downward.

title: Plan to turn Vietnam into strong maritime nation by 2030 cleared
content:
As part of Vietnam’s resolution on turning itself into a strong maritime nation by 2030, it will develop green and smart seaports, its merchant fleet, shipbuilding industries and maritime logistics, while strengthening connectivity between seaports and road, rail, inland waterway and air transport networks. 
The government will review the Master Plan for Vietnam's Seaport System for the 2021-2030 period.

title: Dhaka plans initiative to expand trade, investment with New Zealand
content:
To further strengthen bilateral trade and investment relations, Bangladesh recently discussed with New Zealand Trade and Enterprise (NZTE) an initiative to expand cooperation in several sectors, including green energy, leather, jute and sustainable textiles. 
Bangladesh highlighted opportunities for joint investment, B2B linkages and export expansion in these sectors at a meeting with NZTE representatives.

title: Brazil, Indonesia mull establishing Indonesia-Mercosur PTA
content:
Brazil and Indonesia are mulling over a preferential trade agreement as a first step towards deeper ties and widening market access between Southeast Asia and Latin America, according to Indonesia’s Trade Minister Budi Santoso. 
Santoso discussed the plan with Brazil’s Minister of Development, Industry, Trade and Services Marcio Fernando Elias Rosa in Jaipur, India, recently during a two-day BRICS meeting.

title: 5 apparel hubs gain 5.7% as China, Türkiye lose $8.4 bn
content:
India, Pakistan, Indonesia, Egypt and Morocco raised HS 61-62 apparel exports by 5.7 per cent to $41.68 billion in 2025, while China and Türkiye lost about $8.4 billion.
UNCTAD says announced greenfield projects in textiles, clothing and leather fell 35 per cent as global textile capacity utilisation was 71 per cent.
The next phase of diversification depends on capital following orders.

title: Under Armour cuts 25% more products to save margins. Will it work?
content:
Under Armour plans another 25 per cent SKU cut in 18 months, taking the total reduction to about 40 per cent by end-2028.
It is prioritising full-price sales, cleaner inventory and margins over top-line growth, with annual revenue guidance cut to down mid-single digit.
Analysts flag soft North America and Asia Pacific demand, Nike discounting and mid-market distribution as risks to sales recovery.

title: Can Under Armour revive growth after Q1 FY27 revenue decline?
content:
American sportswear company Under Armour reported a 3 per cent YoY decline in Q1 FY27 revenue to $1.1 billion, as weaker North American and Asian demand weighed on sales. 
The gross margin expanded 590 bps to 54.1 per cent, while net income stood at $1 million. 
The company lowered its FY27 revenue outlook to a mid-single-digit decline amid softer demand globally.

title: Labour compliance puts Bangladesh garment exporters under pressure
content:
Bangladesh’s garment exporters face tougher labour and traceability requirements in the EU and US, with compliance increasingly affecting market access, shipment clearance and buyer decisions. 
Smaller factories could face greater risks from limited compliance capacity, while stronger labour and safety systems may help exporters secure stable buyer relationships and improve competitiveness.
